classification.difficultyReason: Construct the north-referenced walk from two bearings, identify its right triangle, use Pythagoras and inverse tangent, then convert and reverse the final bearing. The direction conversion is the hardest connection and is scaffolded by the earlier triangle parts.

content.prompt: Goran walks from $O$ to $A$, 10 km away, on a true bearing of $300^\circ\mathrm{T}$. He then walks 24 km from $A$ to $B$ on a true bearing of $30^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram to represent Goran’s walk and include the given information.

answer.worked: The first leg goes northwest from $O$ on a bearing of $300^\circ\mathrm{T}$; the second goes northeast from $A$ on a bearing of $030^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

spec.description: Coordinate-derived walk with north arrows at the two bearing origins, clockwise bearing arcs and labelled distances.

answer.worked: The bearing of $O$ from $A$ is $120^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle OAB=120^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the distance between his start and finish points (that is, $OB$).

children.label: d
children.prompt: Calculate the size of $\angle AOB$, correct to 2 decimal places.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Hence calculate the bearing of $O$ from $B$ correct to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$187^\circ\mathrm{T}$

Reverse the bearing from $O$ to $B$ by adding $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
At $O$, the angle from north to $OA$ towards the west is $60^\circ$. Thus the bearing of $B$ from $O$ is
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{10}\right)-60^\circ\\\beta&=7.380135\ldots^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The reverse bearing is
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }O\text{ from }B&=180^\circ+7.380135\ldots^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }O\text{ from }B&\approx187^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
